text:
jo: Quick one - after yesterday's console rollout we saw a surge in reconnects and a correlated quota burn spike at ~03:22 UTC. panels look noisy. anyone else? :eyes:
sam: Saw that. Console routing change introduced sticky-routing fallback to new shard logic. Did that affect session stickiness?
opsbot: alert: streaming.reconnects_rate crossed 2000 (1m) at 2026-04-02T03:23:00Z. :rotating_light:
sre: Can you share the query/panel? Is this sum across shards or per-shard?
jo: It's the "Connections -> Reconnects (1m)" panel: `sum(rate(stream.reconnects[1m])) by (env)` so per-env. When I split by `shard` I see one shard with a 6x spike.
console-eng: We rolled a canary that flips routing to prefer low-cost hosts, and it also changed the fallback order on failure. Might be a timing interaction with our lease expiry.
sam: Repro notes: client reconnects trigger a resume that hits the router. If the router's fallback chooses a different shard while the original lease is still valid, both shards might report a reconnect/resume for the same client before the first shard releases.
product-ux: Is this a UX regression from the console change or an infra bug? Customers saw transient 429s during the spike and some webhooks were delayed.
sre: Likely infra. Two things to investigate: (1) metrics double-counting when handoff happens, (2) router fallback/until-stable causing duplicate reconnect attempts.
jo: I grabbed tracer for a single session: timestamps show client reconnect -> router A accepts -> proxy hands to router B -> both routers emit `reconnect` metric within ~300ms. Logs: ```
2026-04-02T03:22:12Z router=A session=xx reconnect=1 shard=shard-42 owner=router-A
2026-04-02T03:22:12Z router=B session=xx reconnect=1 shard=shard-42 owner=router-B
```
sam: The router code adds `owner` after resolving sticky cookie, but the emitter attaches metrics before owner tag is set when handoff happens. So two metrics with different owner tags collapse in dashboards that don't group by owner.
console-eng: Short-term: we can modify dashboards to `max by (env,shard)` instead of `sum` to reduce duplicate alert noise. Long-term we need router to preserve owner tag or add an `event_id`/idempotency tag emitted by the client side.
sre: Watch out: adding event_id as a tag increases cardinality massively if we keep retention. Better to attach `session_owner` which is stable per session and can be dropped by ingestion TTL.
jo: Also saw spike in quota billing: the quota service counts reconnect attempts per session and sums across replicas. We should enforce a single authoritative admit decision at the ingress so quota is charged once.
opsbot: note: I temporarily muted the reconnect alert for 20m while we triage.
console-eng: Plan: 1) Patch router to add `session_owner` earlier in the flow so emitter includes it (PR planned), 2) Update dashboards to `max` and add a panel note linking to issue, 3) Add a small canary to ensure no perf regressions.
sre: Also add a small jitter when claiming ownership during handoff to reduce race windows; but make sure it doesn't increase tail latency. We'll experiment with 50-100ms jitter in canary.
product-ux: For the console rollout, should we rollback to previous routing until fix? We had a handful of customers affected.
jo: We can pause the canary (we rolled to 10% traffic). Console-eng: I'll pause ramp to 0% and revert the rollout flags for now.
sam: I'll open PR for emitter idempotency tag + router owner preservation. assign to me.
sre: Filing infra ticket #4330 to review quota charge path and canonicalize owner semantics.
jo: Thanks team. Once PRs land let's re-enable canary with stricter telemetry on reconnects and quota burn. :thumbsup:
